program: Medical-bill navigation and consumer health policy
priceScope: Historical matched FY2023 full annual recipient cost against a partial assistance channel; current productivity and policy benefits unknown, not zero, and not a marginal-gift offer.

what: Free Consumer Assistance Program helps people contest bills, denied coverage and eligibility barriers; it does not pay their medical bills.
The charity also advocates for consumer protection and implementation of Colorado health policy with agencies and coalitions.
This historical numerical reference pairs FY2023 costs with 777 annual clients; it is not current productivity, cumulative bills saved or whole-policy expected value.
strengths: Current recipient, free-service route and linked donation intake are identified.
Original three-year IRS costs are checked, including netted fundraising costs.
Actual cash avoidance and full provider/insurer incidence are distinguished from nominal charges written off.
reservations: The observed 777 annual clients are historical and not unique households or causal outcomes; current cohort, local share and utility remain uncertain.
Bills saved are not necessarily otherwise-paid consumption, and the counterparty can lose the same collectible cash.
Whole annual costs fund policy and organizing too; their implemented health and resource effects remain unmeasured rather than assumed zero.

sections.what:
CAP supports billing appeals and applications while policy work addresses affordability, coverage and consumer protections.

Current cumulative counters differ across the same page; neither is used as annual delivered cases.
sections.monitoring:
Seek annual unique clients, actual collected cash avoided, completed appeals and recipients inside the ten-county Denver boundary.

Measure implemented policy changes against agency obligations and alternatives, not only legislation or coalition participation.
sections.qualitative:
Self-appeals, legally required hospital assistance, insurers and other advocates form the counterfactual. Staffing limits can delay responses.

Historical Axis work in southwest Colorado is outside this edition; headquarters do not establish beneficiary geography.
sections.cost:
Matched FY2023 full annual cost is $1,536,690: functional expenses $1,523,080 plus $13,610 netted event costs. Latest FY2024 full cost is $1,801,425 and is a mismatched-vintage sensitivity.

The historical 2023 model uses 777 observed clients, judged 90% unique households, 50% Denver share and 40% additionality. A $2,000 nominal bill reduction × 25% otherwise-paid collection fraction implies $500 cash avoided, not medical retail value.

Positive gains receive a 50% overlap adjustment; $25 access costs and process harms apply to all exposed households. A full $500 provider/insurer loss per changed household is retained without overlap discount.

Policy implementation, attribution, finite duration and delay are missing causal inputs; they are not assigned statewide population benefits. Latest-cost and annual-mean scenarios are sensitivities, not CAP allocations or marginal costs.
sections.funding:
Own donation page links a working EveryAction intake; no transaction was made. Free CAP access is not conditional on giving.

Current grants or appeals do not prove capacity to convert the next unrestricted dollar into incremental completed assistance.

model.costScope: Matched historical FY2023 full annual recipient cost against observed 777 assistance clients; latest FY2024 costs shown as mismatched-vintage sensitivity, not current productivity.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged 0.5 Denver beneficiary share within CBSA19740; statewide work and southwest Colorado pilot are not all local.
model.formula: Health = (N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − all-exposed process harm) × Denver share. Signed resources jointly log changed and other exposed households, with full distinct provider/insurer loss and geography once; price = 10 × C / combined equivalents.
model.counterfactual: Mandated hospital assistance, public eligibility, insurers, self-appeals, other navigators and agency implementation would continue without CCHI.
model.attribution: b=.4 and successful cash recovery=.6 are conditional judgments, not local trial estimates. Wider policy implementation and causal contribution remain unknown.
model.uncertainty: Annual unique cohort, collectibility, utility, local share and policy effects are not empirically calibrated; null, adverse, payer and cost-boundary scenarios expose this.
model.nativeOutcomes: Original 2023 annual report states 777 clients and more than $2M nominal bill savings that year across 48 counties. Annual clients are not deduplicated households or incremental successes. Current and IRS cumulative counters are not annual outcomes.
